21                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

22   Resolution Number 4449, by Senator Carlucci, 

23   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

24   proclaim May 23, 2016, as Haitian Unity Day in 

25   the State of New York.


                                                                2730

 1                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 2   Carlucci.

 3                SENATOR CARLUCCI:   Thank you, 

 4   Mr. President.

 5                It's an absolute honor and a 

 6   privilege to be celebrating an annual tradition 

 7   that we've started here in the Capitol, Haitian 

 8   Unity Day, to celebrate the contributions that 

 9   Haitian Americans have made to our local 

10   communities, to the state, and to our nation.

11                And I have the good fortune and 

12   blessing to represent a district that has one of 

13   the highest numbers of Haitian-Americans per 

14   capita in the nation, and that's something that 

15   we're extremely proud of in Rockland County.

16                And today we have joined with us a 

17   few guests from Rockland that are here 

18   celebrating with us.  And we have in the gallery 

19   Henri Desrosiers, Davidson and Natasha Audin, 

20   Yola Moiso.  And Eudson Francois was here, he had 

21   to leave, with Pastor Nathaniel Demosthene.  

22                And Renold Julien, who's here, who 

23   is the head of the Rockland County Haiti task 

24   force, the Haitian Relief Task Force, and also 

25   the head of Konbit Neg Lakay, where we're going 


                                                                2731

 1   to be having a Haitian unity celebration on 

 2   Thursday.  

 3                So everyone is invited, that's in 

 4   Spring Valley, starting at 5:30 p.m.  We're going 

 5   to be having Haitian cuisine, music.  So we 

 6   anticipate a great turnout, and everybody here is 

 7   welcome.

 8                But we also have with us former 

 9   Rockland County legislator Reverend Jacques 

10   Michel, who gave us an opening prayer this 

11   morning when we did a celebration in 711.

12                But Haitian-Americans have made so 

13   many contributions to pretty much every corner of 

14   our society, whether it's in religion, politics, 

15   medicine, fashion, music, you name it.  And 

16   Haitian-Americans have added and made all of 

17   these things better.

18                Now, we call it Haitian Unity Day 

19   because we think it's very important that we stay 

20   united.  

21                And unfortunately, just a few months 

22   ago, right in Rockland County, we had a 

23   disturbing event where an organization, a 

24   healthcare organization, was advertising to hire 

25   a nurse but they said "No Haitian need apply." 


                                                                2732

 1   Now, obviously we were very disturbed by that.  

 2                And we gathered together and we 

 3   reached out to the Attorney General to say, Look, 

 4   we've got to do something about this.  We've got 

 5   to make sure that this type of discrimination is 

 6   not tolerated this day and age in the State of 

 7   New York or anywhere.

 8                And luckily the Attorney General 

 9   followed through, hit the company with a large 

10   fine -- but more importantly, made them reform 

11   their practices.  Because what we realized is 

12   that even though that was a blatant form of 

13   discrimination, how many times are people being 

14   discriminated against where they don't even know?  

15   Where a customer might say, "Look, I want a 

16   nurse, but not a Haitian nurse," and where a 

17   nurse might not ever know that they were 

18   discriminated against just for being Haitian.

19                So it's important that we celebrate 

20   the contributions that Haitian-Americans have 

21   made, that we stay united and talk about all the 

22   great things that have been added to our state, 

23   to our nation, because of Haitian-American 

24   culture.

25                So I want to thank our guests that 


                                                                2733

 1   are here today, look forward to celebrating with 

 2   you again on Thursday, and thank you again for 

 3   Haitian unity.  

 4                Mr. President, I look forward to all 

 5   of our colleagues cosponsoring the resolution.

 6                Thank you very much.

 7                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 8   Hamilton.

 9                SENATOR HAMILTON:   Mr. President, I 

10   rise in order to honor our visitors today 

11   representing Haitian Unity Day.  

12                As you know we celebrated Flag Day 

13   with City Councilman Mathieu Eugene, the first 

14   Haitian-American elected to the City Council of 

15   New York City.  

16                And when you think about Haiti, I 

17   think about the strong republic that was the 

18   first slave colony to get its independence.  

19   Haiti beat the largest army known to man at the 

20   time, the French army.  And today the spirit of 

21   the hard work of Haitian-Americans in my 

22   district, as far as being small business owners, 

23   is an asset to our community.

24                And when I think of Haiti, I think 

25   of America being great because of the Louisiana 


                                                                2734

 1   Purchase.  The only reason why the Louisiana 

 2   Purchase happened was because Toussaint 

 3   Louverture beat the French in Haiti.  So America 

 4   would not be what it is today if it was not for 

 5   the Haitian-Americans and the great generals who 

 6   fought the French army.  Under duress, with less 

 7   men, less ammunition and arms, but they beat a 

 8   world power at the time.

 9                So today I honor my brothers and 

10   sisters from Haiti.  I want to say bonsoir, you 

11   know, and thank you for coming here today.  

12                And I just want to say when we look 

13   at our history books in the State of New York and 

14   we have the Louisiana Purchase, there's no 

15   reference, there's no reference to Haiti, there's 

16   no reference to the French being beat in Haiti 

17   and the reason the Louisiana Purchase was made 

18   was because of a slave revolt that beat the 

19   French army.  And because of that, it led to 

20   other countries gaining independence from people 

21   who were colonizing countries throughout the 

22   Caribbean.  

23                So Haiti was the first republic to 

24   beat the yoke, to beat the most advanced army of 

25   its time, and we honor you for that.  So I feel 


                                                                2735

 1   that in New York State, in our history books, 

 2   when we mention the Louisiana Purchase, we should 

 3   mention the Haitian revolution and how we beat 

 4   the French and how the Louisiana Purchase was 

 5   done.

 6                We should also acknowledge that 

 7   Haiti was the first republic to beat its 

 8   slavemasters under a brutal system of slavery 

 9   that many died working in the fields.  

10                So I honor the Haitian-Americans in 

11   our country, and I honor the three new 

12   Haitian-American Assemblywoman in the Assembly:  

13   Kimberly Jean-Pierre, Rodneyse Bichotte, and 

14   Michaelle Solages.  

15                So we are seeing the emergence of 

16   Haitian-Americans in New York City, in New York 

17   State, and throughout the world.  

18   Congratulations.  God bless Haiti.  {in Haitian 

19   Creole} 

20                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

21   Sanders.

22                SENATOR SANDERS:   I too must honor 

23   the Haitian people in my district and the nation 

24   and in the world.  But it would not be right to 

25   not point out just two facts.  


                                                                2736

 1                It is true that Haiti defeated the 

 2   armies of France, but it has to be recognized 

 3   that those armies were commanded by one of the 

 4   world's greatest generals.  That was Napoleon.  

 5   That was Napoleon's army.  Which he is of course 

 6   studied every place where we study the military 

 7   because he was one of the world's greatest minds 

 8   in terms of military.  So if you beat the world's 

 9   greatest mind in military, in my books that makes 

10   you the greatest of the greatest.

11                There I go thinking again.

12                It would also -- right now, when we 

13   think of Haiti, we think of many different 

14   things, but we also think of a poor country.  It 

15   would not be this poor had they not had to pay 

16   for their own freedom.  Even after they won, they 

17   were forced to literally pay for the right to be 

18   free.  They did pay.  They already paid in blood, 

19   now they had to pay in treasure.

20                I believe that it is most 

21   appropriate that the monies that were taken from 

22   the Haitian people should be given back to the 

23   Haitian people, that the governments that took 

24   from Haiti need to give back to it.  Then we can 

25   stop thinking of Haiti as a poor country and we 


                                                                2737

 1   can see it as the rich country that it really is, 

 2   and they would have enough money to do what they 

 3   need to do and not need the charity of anyone.  

 4   The Haitian people do not want charity, they want 

 5   parity.

 6                Thank you very much for being here.  

 7   Thank you for being in New York State.  Thank you 

 8   for being in my district, which has the greatest 

 9   Haitian people -- well --

10                SENATOR HAMILTON:   Brooklyn!  

11                (Laughter.)

12                SENATOR SANDERS:   Of course, 

13   Brooklyn is a fine place.  But I'm speaking of 

14   the greatest, and that of course is Southeast 

15   Queens.  And I encourage you all to come to 

16   Southeast Queens right after my friend here 

17   comes.

18                So having said that, Mr. President, 

19   I will sit down and speak no more.

20                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

21   Hassell-Thompson.

22                SENATOR HASSELL-THOMPSON:   Thank 

23   you, Mr. President.

24                Several of the delegation are sort 

25   of lost in the hall.  I was out in the hall 


                                                                2738

 1   greeting them, and many of them are legislators 

 2   from Haiti, representatives.  And I'm sorry 

 3   somehow they didn't make it to the gallery.  

 4                But I am very pleased to stand with 

 5   my colleagues today to congratulate you and thank 

 6   you for coming to our chambers and being with us 

 7   today.

 8                I know that Brooklyn has the largest 

 9   number.  I know that Senator Sanders believes 

10   that he has the best people.  But if you saw the 

11   devotion with which I am held with those that 

12   live in my district, you would understand that 

13   mine are par excellence.

14                But the reality is my first visit to 

15   Haiti was in 1972, and it was right after tourism 

16   first opened.  And I had two very young children, 

17   a 4-year-old and a 6-year-old.  And when I 

18   returned home, my husband said:  "Oh, I did not 

19   know that the politics was such.  Why would you 

20   take our children to Haiti?"  And I said, "I 

21   needed our children to be in an environment that 

22   was controlled by people of color, the people 

23   that looked like them, and so that they would 

24   understand that what it meant to really be free.

25                And so you have continued to 


                                                                2739

 1   struggle.  And certainly I had the grand 

 2   opportunity during the devastation that you 

 3   experienced to be a part of the statewide effort 

 4   for the Haiti disaster.  And only two weeks ago, 

 5   I just took down that poster that we had.  And I 

 6   understand one thing, though.  There are still 

 7   people living in tents since that disaster.  And 

 8   the terrible things that have happened -- first 

 9   the hurricane came before the earthquake.  

10   Everybody thinks about the earthquake, but I was 

11   familiar with what -- the devastation that you 

12   experienced in terms of the first real crops that 

13   you had after that Hurricane Hanna.

14                And so I continue to be very much a 

15   part of the delegation that wants to help to 

16   rebuild and restore.  And two of my very young 

17   friends who have grown up with my children have 

18   returned to Haiti, which is their homeland, to 

19   help to rebuild and to restore.  

20                So there is hope.  Our young people 

21   are returning to Haiti to help to rebuild and to 

22   bring your country back after its successive 

23   devastations.  But the bravery with which you 

24   face the challenges that continue to mark your 

25   country, for that I have a great deal of respect 


                                                                2740

 1   and regard.  

 2                And I am very appreciative that the 

 3   delegation finally found their way to the 

 4   gallery.  And I wanted to publicly welcome all of 

 5   you to the State of New York, the greatest state 

 6   in the world.

 7                (Applause from gallery.)

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   Senator 

 9   Parker.  

10                SENATOR PARKER:   Thank you, 

11   Mr. President.  On the resolution.

12                ACTING PRESIDENT GRIFFO:   On the 

13   resolution.

14                SENATOR PARKER:   I want to stand 

15   and add my voice to those today in this chamber 

16   who are celebrating Haitian Flag Day, which was 

17   May 18th.  

18                And we celebrate this holiday in my 

19   district very hard, Mr. President.  I don't know 

20   if you know I represent the largest concentration 

21   of the Haitian people outside of Haiti in the 

22   entire world -- a larger number in Florida, a 

23   larger concentration in my district.  

24                And what we find when we look at the 

25   history of this great island is it is a history 


                                                                2741

 1   that resembles the history of the United States.  

 2   It's a history of people who were yearning to be 

 3   free, who were looking for life, liberty and the 

 4   pursuit of happiness.  And had to literally fight 

 5   their oppressors in the French in order to make 

 6   that happen.

 7                So much so that when they threw them 

 8   out the first time, the French came back and they 

 9   had to burn down Port-au-Prince in order to keep 

10   them out the second time.  And so that's the kind 

11   of determination that we see in the folks from 

12   this wonderful island.  

13                I had a great opportunity to visit 

14   Haiti this past November and spend some time in 

15   Port-au-Prince during the election and to see, in 

16   a place that has gone through so much hardship, 

17   the real commitment to building democracy.  A 

18   real democratic country is really, really 

19   amazing.  

20                And so I want to acknowledge the 

21   delegation that is here from Haiti, many of which 

22   are elected officials, members of their 

23   parliament and some of their local leaders who 

24   have joined us and thank them for coming and 

25   honoring us with their presence.  And really, 


                                                                2742

 1   when we talk about Haiti, we should always 

 2   remember they are the first place to get freedom 

 3   in the Western Hemisphere.  

 4                And so really, you know, in a lot of 

 5   ways it was Haiti that led the way for the U.S. 

 6   to seek its freedom.  And so we thank you for all 

 7   that you've done for this world, but then also 

 8   what you've done for the people of the State of 

 9   New York.

10                We have a number of very notable 

11   people of Haitian descent, most notably in the
